_comment: Flexion-dependent marker slide, calibrated on P10/Trial2_handsonly.
Markers are taped to the dorsum, and the dorsal surface over a flexed
knuckle is longer than over an extended one, so a marker slides DISTALLY
along its segment as the governing joint flexes. Measured over the whole
trial: MCP->PIP marker spacing grows 7-10mm (~20%) from extension to full
flexion, correlating +0.80..+0.85 with flexion angle, while the palm
control grows 1.3mm (+0.22). Bone cannot lengthen; this is skin.
A fixed-vertex attachment cannot represent that -- the marker does stay
at a fixed material point on real skin, but MANO's linear blend skinning
does not reproduce how far that skin slides over a flexing joint. Hence
the residual pattern: middle/ring MCPs over-rotate ~20 deg to reach
markers that separated more than the mesh stretches, and finger-3 markers
(furthest along the chain, accumulating every segment's stretch) sit
13-20mm out even in otherwise good frames.
slope_mm_per_deg: distal slide along the segment per degree of flexion of
the governing joint. r2 is from the linear fit used to derive it -- the
finger-2 markers are well modelled (0.64-0.73), the finger-3 markers are
not (0.06-0.43), so expect this to do real work only on finger 2.
Ring3 at r2=0.06 is noise and is left at zero.

ref_deg: the flexion ALREADY PRESENT in the static, which is where the attachments were calibrated. The static is not an extended hand -- it carries 19-28 deg of MCP flexion -- so the slide must be applied relative to this, not from zero. Applying it from zero double-counts the stretch already baked into the attachment and made the fit worse (fingers 6.65 -> 8.36mm), which is how this was found.
